messages:
Kait (Product): quick design check — putting this in front of UX + eng. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd/run-summary-cards Kait (Product): main questions: 1) skeleton/loading state for run-summary cards (list view) — do we keep a full shimmer or collapse to compact placeholders? 2) screen-reader announce behavior for run progress vs final result (NVDA/VoiceOver). 3) approval CTA state while a run is in progress — should it be disabled, and how do we surface why? Miguel (Designer): attaching mock: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd/run-summary-cards?node-id=42 Miguel (Designer): proposal: keep list density but make skeletons compact — 3 grey lines + small circular avatar placeholder + ghosted action button. On load complete card expands animation to full card. Miguel (Designer): microcopy idea for disabled CTA: "Preview in progress — approvals locked" (tooltip: "Approvals re-enabled when preview completes") :lock: Sam (Frontend): implementation notes — prefer not to use aria-live for every skeleton state (will be noisy). We can hide skeletons from AT using aria-hidden="true" and only announce the final state. Sam (Frontend): for announcing final result we can use a single live region in the page shell. Example: ```
// when run completes: document.getElementById('run-live').textContent = 'Run "smoke-test" complete: 12/12 succeeded'; ``` This avoids duplicate announcements when multiple cards update quickly. Rina (Accessibility): agree with Sam. Important: do not put skeletons in an aria-live region. Instead: - set skeletons aria-hidden="true" so they don't get read - use role="status" + aria-live="polite" only for final success/failure messages - for failures include a short text summary and a link with focusable id that can be referenced by aria-describedby on the notification Rina (Accessibility): keyboard focus rule: if the user initiated the run (clicked "Run"), shift focus to the toast/notification when it finishes. If the run was automatic/background, do NOT steal focus — just update the live region. Asha (PM): regarding approvals: product concern is accidental approvals during incomplete previews. So yes, disable primary Approve while run is active. But can we add a small fallback for power users? maybe an "Approve draft" (no final commitment) that is allowed while previewing. Miguel (Designer): UX for that: primary CTA disabled + secondary "Approve draft" (ghost) visible. Draft approval copy: "Mark as draft approval — will not trigger rollout". Keep tertiary overflow for advanced actions. Sam (Frontend): edge-case: if user navigates away and returns while run is in progress, we should keep state consistent. Live region should not re-announce when route changes back; guard updates by tracking last-announced run id. Rina (Accessibility): testing: we need explicit test cases in the eval checklist: VoiceOver macOS, NVDA latest, TalkBack (android) for announcements and focus behavior. Also include keyboard-only flow for approve/draft/tooltip. deploy-bot: staging build 782 passed — snapshot tests for run-summary-card skeletons included :white_check_mark: Kait (Product): next steps: Miguel to update Figma with compact skeleton + disabled CTA tooltip copy. Sam to open a frontend ticket with sample live-region code and focus rules. Rina to add accessibility checklist items and pair test. Asha to spec "Approve draft" rules for product/PR. Kait (Product): adding acceptance criteria in the ticket: 1) skeletons are aria-hidden; 2) final result announced once via page live region; 3) primary Approve disabled during run with tooltip copy; 4) optional "Approve draft" available and described. Please add links to tickets when created. :thumbsup: Miguel (Designer): noted. will push updated frames by EOD. :eyes: Sam (Frontend): will create PR draft and tag @Rina for test pairing. Rina (Accessibility): will add checklist and propose manual test steps. Asha (PM): love this — thanks all. quick follow-up: include a line in the release notes about the disabled-approve behavior. Kait (Product): thanks everyone — moving this to the design handoff board.
